2609.21383.title: Prediction Dynamics in Depth-Recurrent Language Models
2609.21383.paper_summary: Depth-recurrent language models refine predictions through repeated latent updates. Why can intermediate answers agree with the endpoint while their scores continue to change? We derive a sharp margin characterization that decomposes the conservatism of a magnitude bound into common translation, direction relative to the winner, and the pairing of each competitor's update with its score gap. Across Huginn-3.5B and Ouro-1.4B, accounting for update direction and competitor pairing reduces the mean earliest qualifying depth by a further 22.5-34.4% of the total depth beyond translation removal under full answer-text scoring. This retrospective comparison uses completed trajectories. Substantial contributions also occur under label scoring. For shared predictive distributions, we separate common and contrast motion orthogonally and express the common component through candidate-set mass and within-set concentration. Common and contrast energies can attenuate at different rates, allowing a growing preference-change share to coexist with shrinking absolute updates. These findings explain finite-depth answer preservation through the geometry and composition of observed score changes.
2609.21383.paper_summary_zh: 深度重複語言模型通過重複的潛在更新來精煉預測。為什麼中間答案可以與最終結果一致，而它們的分數仍然不斷變化？我們推導出了一個明確的邊際特徵，將幅度界限的保守性分解為共同翻譯、相對於獲勝者的方向，以及每個競爭者的更新與其分數差距的配對。在 Huginn-3.5B 和 Ouro-1.4B 中，考慮更新方向和競爭者配對使得平均最早合格深度進一步減少了 22.5-34.4% 的總深度，這是在完全答案文本評分下去除翻譯的情況下。這一回顧性比較使用了已完成的軌跡。在標籤評分下也有顯著的貢獻。對於共享的預測分佈，我們將共同運動和對比運動正交分開，並通過候選集質量和集內集中度來表達共同成分。共同能量和對比能量可以以不同的速率衰減，允許不斷增長的偏好變化份額與縮小的絕對更新共存。這些發現解釋了通過觀察到的分數變化的幾何和組成來保持有限深度答案的原因。
2609.21383.author: Xinyue Luo et.al.
